name: Germany
standard: EN 301 549 (currently V3.2.1, WCAG 2.1 AA) via BITV 2.0 §3; plus German Sign Language and Easy Language explanations

laws.summary: Federal public bodies must design websites and mobile apps to be barrier-free.
Sets the technical standard, accessibility statement, feedback and Sign/Easy Language duties for federal bodies.
Transposes the EAA for private-sector products and services, in force from 2025-06-28.

policy_docs.title: MLBF — Länder market surveillance for BFSG

applies_to: BGG/BITV 2.0: federal public bodies. Each of the 16 Länder has its own accessibility law and ordinance for state and municipal bodies. BFSG: private economic operators of EAA products and services.
exceptions: WAD content exceptions and disproportionate burden as transposed
requires: Meet harmonised standards in the OJ (EN 301 549) or state of the art (BITV §3)
Homepage explanations in German Sign Language and Leichte Sprache (BITV §4)
Accessibility statement, machine-readable and reachable from every page, updated annually (BITV §7)
Electronic feedback contact reachable from every page or app navigation (BITV §7(2))
mobile: explicit — BGG §12a and BITV 2.0 cover mobile applications; BFSG covers EAA app-based services.
procurement: BGG requires barrier-free IT when federal bodies procure new IT; BFSG covers products and services supplied to consumers.
enforcement: BFIT-Bund (at Deutsche Rentenversicherung Knappschaft-Bahn-See) monitors federal sites. The Schlichtungsstelle BGG at the Federal Disability Commissioner handles complaints. MLBF (Magdeburg, operating since 2025-09-26) is market surveillance for BFSG and takes consumer reports.
notes: BFIT-Bund, the Schlichtungsstelle and the MLBF start date (2025-09-26) were confirmed via search-result summaries of bundesfachstelle-barrierefreiheit.de and state sites; the MLBF page itself was opened. The BGG and BFSG index URLs are gesetze-im-internet.de roots; a guessed BFSG deep link returned 404.
